steps.description: Filter the 12,000-gene matrix to genes with at least 10 counts in at least 1 sample (the smallest group size here is 1), and report how many genes pass. Estimate median-of-ratios size factors with DESeq2 on the filtered matrix and report both size factors. Set control as the explicit reference level so a positive value means higher in treated; name the contrast as condition, treated (numerator) vs control (denominator) in the output. steps.description: Take the full table of filtered, tested genes from T1S2 — not a thresholded subset — and rank every gene by its descriptive log2 fold change (treated vs control). plan.title: Liver treated vs control: descriptive 1v1 fold changes
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a single gene-symbol x sample raw count matrix from salmon (counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 2 samples) with a 2-row metadata table declaring one treated and one control human liver sample. The research question asks which genes are differentially expressed between the two. With one sample per condition there is no within-group replication, so no dispersion can be estimated and no p-value has an inferential basis (knowledge rule R-0003). The plan therefore does NOT fit an inferential test: it produces sample-structure QC and library-size diagnostics (T1S1), a low-count filter with median-of-ratios size factors and a descriptive log2 fold change table for treated vs control (T1S2, reference level control set explicitly so a positive log2FC means higher in treated), a descriptive preranked gene set enrichment ranked by that log2 fold change against human Hallmark, then Reactome and WikiPathways with no set-level p-value taken as evidence (T2S1), and a report that states the design limitation, the ranking metric, the collection releases, and the reproducibility record (T1S3). The shrinkage and multiple-testing steps of a standard DE procedure are deliberately absent because the flagged design removes inference; the output is a ranked candidate list for a follow-up experiment with biological replicates (minimum 3 per condition), not a set of differentially expressed genes.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), library sizes, sample distance
Low count filter: at least 10 counts in at least 1 sample
Explicit reference level control, contrast treated vs control (descriptive only)
Descriptive log fold changes only, no inferential test
fgsea preranked GSEA ranked by descriptive log2 fold change, Hallmark then Reactome and WikiPathways

steps.description: Assemble a single report from T1S1, T1S2, and T2S1. Lead with the limitation: the dataset has one treated and one control liver sample, so no gene can be called differentially expressed and no p-value is reported anywhere in this analysis; what follows is a descriptive ranking. Then give: the QC summary (library sizes, detected genes, between-sample distance, liver-identity check); the number of genes tested after the >=10-count filter out of 12,000; the size factors; the contrast definition (condition: treated vs control, reference control) and the sign convention; the top candidate genes by absolute descriptive log2 fold change above the expression floor, with their normalized counts in both samples shown beside every fold change so a reader can see the evidence directly; the count of genes flagged as noise-dominated; and the descriptive pathway ordering per collection with leading-edge genes, marking overlapping leading edges. State the gene set database and release, the ranking metric, the universe, and the size window for each enrichment. Include the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, the random seed used by fgsea, and the version of each gene set collection. Close with the concrete design that would answer the research question: at least 3 and preferably 5 or more biological replicates per condition, which would permit a negative binomial model with dispersion estimation, apeglm shrinkage, and Benjamini-Hochberg control. Do not include a volcano plot, a significance threshold, or any table column named padj/FDR/pvalue.
steps.context: The synthesizer downstream reads this report. Its framing determines whether a reader treats the output as a gene list or as a candidate ranking, so the limitation must be first and unqualified.
acceptance_criteria: Report opens with the no-replication limitation and the statement that no differentially expressed genes are called
No p-value, adjusted p-value, FDR, or significance threshold appears in any table or figure of the report
Genes tested after filtering, both size factors, and the contrast with its sign convention are stated
Top candidate genes shown with their normalized counts in both samples beside the log2 fold change
Per-collection enrichment reporting includes database, release, ranking metric, universe, and size window, plus leading-edge genes
Reproducibility record present: sessionInfo, package versions, fgsea seed, gene set collection versions
Closes with the explicit replicate requirement (>=3, preferably >=5, per condition) and the inferential procedure that would then apply
constraints: report: reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions, collection_version
report: leading_edge listed per reported set
report: enrichment_caveat = method_dependence stated
report: fields = method, package versions, design, filter thresholds, n_tested, session_info
Do not produce a volcano plot or any figure whose axis is a p-value
caveats: The temptation to present the top fold-change genes as a result is the main failure mode of this analysis; every table must carry the descriptive label

grounding.reason: Report content follows R-0041 (method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested), R-0051 (collection, release, metric, universe, size window), R-0105 (leading edge per set), R-0055 (method dependence) and R-0086 (reproducibility record), with the R-0003 no-replication statement carried into the framing.
